correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the exact partial- and full-feedback response sets on a complete multipartite graph. Full feedback is handled by a one-cop sweep of a fixed part. Partial-feedback upper bounds are one-round separating probe sets; lower bounds give explicit adversarial response vectors that preserve two candidates in distinct parts, whose closed neighborhoods recontaminate the entire graph. All boundary cases \(s=1\), \(s=2\), and \(s\ge3\) are covered. An independent finite-state checker exhaustively confirms all multipartitions of total order at most eight; the computation is a stress test rather than the proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification on a canonical graph family for a newly introduced pursuit-evasion invariant. It exhibits a sharp structural phase change: the published complete-bipartite partial-feedback value can be arbitrarily large, while any complete multipartite graph with at least three parts has value at most three. The result also supplies matching one-round strategies and an explicit perpetual-reset robber strategy, clarifying the mechanism rather than only reporting parameter values.
